room: The visitor is inside his painting of his bedroom in the Yellow House in Arles. This is the third version, painted in 1889 at the asylum in Saint-Rémy from his first canvas of 1888. He painted it to give a feeling of complete rest: flat colour without shadows, like a Japanese print, and pairs of opposite colours that make each other stronger (violet walls against yellow wood, a scarlet blanket against green sheets, a blue basin on an orange table). The walls were violet and have faded towards blue.

objects.what: the rush chair at the front, by the wall
objects.knows: He painted the chairs fresh butter yellow, the same yellow as the bed, so the furniture reads as one family against the violet walls. The rush seat is a few thick strokes. A plain chair stood for a simple, honest life; he also painted his own chair on its own.

objects.what: the second rush chair, by the bed
objects.knows: It makes a pair with the first chair. He painted this room in twos: two chairs, two pillows, two portraits. It is the room of a man hoping a friend, Gauguin, would come and share the house.

objects.what: the pillow at the head of the bed
objects.knows: The pillows and sheet are a very light lemon green, so the scarlet blanket glows against them: red and green, opposite colours, side by side. He wanted the bed to look like sleep itself.

objects.what: the second pillow on the bed
objects.knows: A pair with the first pillow. Light colours on the bed and strong ones around it, so the eye comes to rest there.

objects.what: the straw hat from the peg rail
objects.knows: His straw hat, a small spot of yellow among the darker clothes on the pegs. He kept the hanging things to a few strokes so they don't break the calm of the wall.

objects.what: the blue jug from the basin
objects.knows: He put the cool blue jug and basin on the orange table on purpose: blue against orange, so that small corner sings. Simple shapes with dark outlines, like in a Japanese print.

objects.what: the carafe from the washstand
objects.knows: The carafe is a pale green-blue against the orange table and the violet wall: a few cool notes that keep the warm corner from getting heavy.

objects.what: the glass tumbler from the washstand
objects.knows: A small glass by the carafe, a touch of pale light. Even the little things on the washstand are there to balance the colour of that corner.

objects.what: the tall glass bottle from the washstand
objects.knows: Two small bottles on the washstand, painted in a few quick strokes. He put in the ordinary things of his room because the painting is about a simple life, with nothing hidden.

objects.what: the short glass bottle from the washstand
objects.knows: The second, shorter bottle: small pale spots that carry the light across the table.

objects.what: the soap dish from the washstand
objects.knows: A little dish for the soap, a few strokes of colour. Nothing in the room is fancy, and that is the point: a plain room made restful by colour alone.

objects.what: the clothes brush from the washstand
objects.knows: He painted the small, plain things with the same care as the bed: the room is a portrait of how he lived.

objects.what: the big wooden bed
objects.knows: The heart of the painting: a big bed of solid wood in butter yellow, with lemon-green sheets and a scarlet blanket. He wanted it to say sleep and rest, and made it heavy and sturdy so it feels safe.

objects.what: the small orange washstand
objects.knows: He painted the dressing table orange and set a blue basin and jug on it: orange against blue, opposite colours that make each other brighter.

objects.what: the blue washbasin
objects.knows: The blue basin on the orange table, one of the room's pairs of opposite colours, with the blue jug standing in it.

objects.what: the towel hanging by the door
objects.knows: A pale towel on a nail by the door, with a few stripes of colour: a quiet vertical shape beside the busy washstand.

objects.what: the peg rail with his clothes
objects.knows: The pegs with his clothes and straw hat. He showed that he owned little: a few things hung up, painted with a few strokes.

objects.what: the green window
objects.knows: He painted the window green and half open, and the light without shadows, flat like a Japanese print, so nothing in the room feels dramatic.

objects.what: the door on the left
objects.knows: He painted the doors lilac. One led to the stairs, the other to the guest room he made ready for Gauguin.

objects.what: the door behind the bed
objects.knows: The other lilac door, closing the room in so it feels sheltered.

objects.what: the small landscape above the pegs
objects.knows: A small landscape over the bed, a tree in a field: a bit of the outdoors he loved, brought into the room.

objects.what: the portrait of a bearded man on the wall
objects.knows: In this version he hung his own self-portrait over the bed. In the first version the portraits were of friends.

objects.what: the portrait of a woman on the wall
objects.knows: A portrait of a woman beside his own. Who she is isn't certain.

objects.what: the pale picture pinned to the wall
objects.knows: One of two pale works on paper pinned to the wall, drawings or prints: a quiet pale yellow against the violet.

objects.what: the second pale picture on the wall
objects.knows: The second one, beside it: they make a pair, like everything else in this room.
